correctness.rationale: PASS. The domain is real symmetric 2x2 matrices, the nearest positive-semidefinite projection is Frobenius, and input/output norms on the three coordinates (a,c,b) count b once. The Frobenius-isometric transformation to a Lorentz cone yields the mixed-sector Jacobian affine in s=T/r. Its two endpoint matrices are the rank-one oblique projection vf^T and its complement, f^Tv=1, v=(t,1-t,q), f=(t,1-t,2q), q^2=t(1-t). Explicit 3x3 row/column absolute sums give the sharp 3/2 ℓ_1 and ℓ_∞ bounds; the two oblique complementary operators have equal Hilbert norms and squared norm (1-q^2)(1+2q^2)≤9/8. Convexity controls intermediate Jacobians, integration along generic segments and continuity handle switching boundaries. The offdiagonal scaling pair attains ℓ_1, and derivatives as s↑1 with q=1/2 give sharp remaining constants. Independent t-grid endpoint 3-norm calculations corroborated the matrices; the proof, not the sample grid, covers the continuum.
residual_risks: No assertion for complex matrices, n>2, other p, or independent-entry-metric nearest projection.
Finite endpoint sampling is diagnostic; continuum relies on scalar inequalities and segment integration.
